title: Vision logs can persist sensitive screenshot-derived text
reasoning: This feature processes screenshots/images that may contain private UI text. InternVL logs up to 1000 characters of the raw model response at warning level and logs the full output when coordinate parsing fails; Venus does the same. The shared chat helper also logs the full chat response. For image-question APIs, responses may contain OCR-like descriptions or user-visible data from the screenshot, so these logs can persist sensitive screen contents in backend logs. The code already hashes/sanitizes the user instruction for one log path, which suggests logs are expected to avoid raw user/image-derived content, but the model responses bypass that protection.
recommendation: Do not log raw vision model responses by default. Log only bounded metadata such as response length, a stable hash, parse status, and perhaps a very short redacted preview behind an explicit debug flag. Also avoid logging full unparsed output on parse failures.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/backend/test_vision_service.py only covers VisionService initialization, provider selection, and unload state; it does not exercise provider inference logging or assert redaction behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add focused provider/helper tests with a fake model response containing a sentinel secret and assert normal/error logs do not include the sentinel while still recording parse success/failure metadata.
minimumFixScope: Update InternVL, Venus, and shared runtime helper logging for raw model responses and parse failures; add redaction-focused tests around those log paths.
